text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: luminar-prod (VPC private) — NLB target health failing in us-east-1, spike in 502s across dedicated pool. Alert: NLB_HEALTH_UNHEALTHY (alert id: I-9c3f2). Auto-escalation to oncall.
alice (oncall): ack, taking. putting pager channel into focus. starting checklist.
ben (netops): seeing consistent TargetHealth -> unhealthy (code: 502) across tgs-arn: arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:123456:targetgroup/tg-luminar/abcd1234. NLB healthcheck reports TCP 443 failing. Health check source IPs look nonstandard — could be SG or host-level reject.
carla (sre): customer Helana reported increased inference errors ~ 09:12 UTC. Logs show upstream 502 from runtime on nodes behind NLB. No recent deploys in the last 2 hours.
helena (customer-ops): Luminar SRE says about 30-40% of requests 502, some requests time out. Customer SLA impact: degraded for all enterprise accounts in us-east-1. They're actively seeing UX errors.
dan (eng-platform): quick checks: are instances passing health locally? run on a host: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:8080/health` — want 200. Also `sudo iptables -L -n` in case SG rules were pushed incorrectly.
alice (oncall): running the local check on i-0abcde12345: `curl` returns 200 locally. That implies inbound from NLB path is blocked or service returning 502 when proxied.
ben (netops): pulled the SGs for the target instances: sg-03f1ab2c currently allows traffic from 10.0.0.0/16 only (internal). NLB nodes come from elastic IP ranges in the VPC subnets; I suspect a config drift: terraform applied a stricter CIDR. NLB health checks originate from the NLB nodes, which are in the subnet range 10.0.8.0/24 — not covered by sg-03f1ab2c.
carla (sre): that matches: locally ok, but from NLB we get connection reset -> NLB marks target unhealthy -> 502 for client requests. Can we temporarily open the SG to include the NLB subnets while we remediate?
alice (oncall): propose temporary rule: allow tcp 8080 from 10.0.8.0/24 to sg-03f1ab2c. If everyone agrees I'll apply via console/cli and monitor.
ben (netops): +1. I'll prepare the aws cli command. CLI snippet:
```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-03f1ab2c --protocol tcp --port 8080 --cidr 10.0.8.0/24 --description "temp allow NLB healthchecks"
```
dan (eng-platform): also capture current target health before change: `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:123456:targetgroup/tg-luminar/abcd1234` — save output.
alice (oncall): applying SG change now. Will also log the change in the ticket. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ben (netops): change applied (sg-03f1ab2c + ingress tcp 8080 10.0.8.0/24). Tag: incident=6267891234 temp=true owner=netops.
incident-bot: Deployment guardrail: security group change recorded by audit: change-id C-7890. Automatic note will remove rule after 30m unless extended.
carla (sre): watching target health... `describe-target-health` now shows targets draining -> initial healthy checks passing, health -> healthy for az-a nodes. Client 502 rate dropping.
helena (customer-ops): Luminar confirms reduced errors after 09:21 UTC. They still see occasional 502s but much less frequent. Customer thanks the team; will update internal incident channel.
alice (oncall): good. keeping rule open for now while we validate. Next step: reconcile terraform/security automation to include NLB subnets in SG rule to avoid drift. Also investigate why change wasn't in IaC.
dan (eng-platform): action items: 1) add explicit NLB subnet cidrs to the security module for luminar-target-sg; 2) patch automation tests to validate sg contains healthcheck ranges; 3) schedule a postmortem with Luminar for tomorrow.
ben (netops): creating short-lived runbook entry in runbooks/network/nlb-healthcheck-sg.md with steps we executed and the AWS CLI snippets. Will link ticket.
carla (sre): I'll keep monitoring for 15m. If any targets go unhealthy again, fallback plan: update Route53 weighted record to shift 100% traffic to luminar-prod-alb (alternate ALB in same region) while we fully remediate.
alice (oncall): documenting customer impact: Luminar enterprise accounts experienced 09:11-09:21 UTC degradation, 35% 502 peak, estimated 12 minutes. No data exfiltration. Affected model inference endpoints only in us-east-1.
helena (customer-ops): sent an incident update to Luminar: summary + mitigation + ETA for postmortem. They've acknowledged and requested the PM.
ben (netops): scheduling the IaC fix PR now. I'll include an automated test that fails if the SG lacks the VPC NLB subnet ranges. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1723
carla (sre): health is stable for 5m, 200 responses at probe. I'll mark the incident mitigated in the tracker but keep the channel open until SG is reconciled.
alice (oncall): mitigation confirmed. temporary SG rule will be auto-removed at +30m (09:51 UTC) unless we extend. If IaC PR merges, we will remove temp rule before autopurge and rely on IaC-managed SG.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident mitigated (I-9c3f2) — status: recovered. Runbook recommended: include SG verification preflight for all VPC private NLB rollouts. Owner: ben (netops). Follow-up: postmortem assigned to carla (sre), dan (eng-platform).
